details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:539–590 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: _summarize_final_merge_blockers still summarizes all non-acceptable check-runs, so the Layer-2 alert can label advisory failures like Copilot as blockers even when Layer-1 would ignore them.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers agreed the operator-facing “Blocking check-runs” output can misattribute the real merge stall and send debugging effort toward a non-blocking check.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:571–578 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: _clear_final_merge_ineligibility_state is defined but never called, while the merge-success path inlines the same state-clearing jq mutation.
  WHY: This is dead code with a misleading docstring, creating maintenance confusion even though the current inline clearing works.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:541–564 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The final_pr parameter is captured by _summarize_final_merge_blockers but never referenced in the function body.
  WHY: The signature suggests the PR number matters, but the implementation silently ignores it, which is a maintenance hazard.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:255–370 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: _pr_checks_completed now changes behavior globally for all legacy callers, not just the final-merge gate, by switching them to the required-checks filter.
  WHY: This expands Layer-1 semantics onto other merge paths and can alter wave PR behavior compared with the previous “all check-runs must pass” gate.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9665, 11320, 11806, 12632, 12686, 12950, 13041 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Legacy _pr_checks_completed call sites now trigger extra PR metadata and branch-protection API lookups when base_ref is omitted.
  WHY: The behavior is correct but increases API usage on the poll path, which multiple reviewers noted as an avoidable cost.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:466–530, 6444–6458 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: State file updates in the alert path and merge-success path use read-modify-write jq/mv sequences without any locking or version check.
  WHY: Concurrent poll cycles can race and produce duplicate alerts, lost clock resets, or stale final_merge_ineligible_alert_sent_for_sha values.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:549–590 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: _summarize_final_merge_blockers can collapse to an empty string on API or jq failures, leaving the alert with an uninformative blocker summary.
  WHY: When check-run collection fails or times out, operators get a vague “unknown” blocker line instead of actionable failure details.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:434 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: An empty required_status_checks.contexts list from branch protection is treated as an allow-all sentinel.
  WHY: This ignores an explicitly empty server-side required list and falls back to env/default behavior instead of honoring the branch-protection result.
- agents.md:200 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new stable log prefix was added without a legacy alias or migration note.
  WHY: Downstream log parsers keyed to the prior FINAL_MERGE_* prefixes can miss the new alert line until updated.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: _summarize_final_merge_blockers, lines 539–568, specifically the jq filter at lines 555–563
  Problem: The function uses the legacy "every check-run" filter — it selects ALL check-runs whose conclusion is not in {success, neutral, skipped, cancelled} — rather than scoping to the Layer 1 required set.
  Why it fails at runtime: The alert can mark a non-required advisory failure as a blocker, misleading operators about what is actually preventing the merge.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: _clear_final_merge_ineligibility_state, lines 571–578
  Problem: The function is defined but has zero call sites, while the merge-success path in mark_validation_complete inlines the same jq mutation directly.
  Why it fails at runtime: This does not cause a runtime failure, but dead code with a misleading docstring creates a maintenance hazard and can confuse future debugging.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: _summarize_final_merge_blockers, line 541 (local final_pr="$1")
  Problem: The final_pr parameter is captured but never referenced in the function body.
  Why it fails at runtime: The signature suggests the PR number matters, but the implementation silently ignores it, which is a latent maintenance risk.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: Legacy callers of _pr_checks_completed at lines 9665, 11320, 11806, 12632, 12686, 12950, 13041 (1-arg and 2-arg call patterns)
  Problem: Seven legacy call sites invoke _pr_checks_completed without the new third base_ref argument, causing extra PR fetches and branch-protection lookups on the new path.
  Why it fails at runtime: Behavior remains correct, but the added API traffic is an avoidable cost on each poll tick.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: _pr_checks_completed, lines 255–370
  Problem: The Layer 1 rewrite changes _pr_checks_completed globally for all legacy callers, not just the final-merge gate.
  Why it fails at runtime: This expands the new required-checks semantics onto other merge paths and can change wave PR behavior relative to the previous gate.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line: _summarize_final_merge_blockers (lines ~539-568)
  Problem: The blocker summary function uses the legacy "every check-run" filter rather than the Layer-1 required-set filter.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators may spend time fixing a non-blocking check while the real blocker remains unaddressed.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh  
  Line: _clear_final_merge_ineligibility_state (lines ~571-578)
  Problem: This helper function is defined but never called; the merge-success path in mark_validation_complete inlines the jq mutations directly.
  Why it fails at runtime: Does not cause functional failure, but dead code with misleading documentation creates maintenance confusion.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line: _check_final_merge_ineligibility_alert and state file updates (lines ~466-530, ~6444-6458)
  Problem: Multiple jq read-modify-write sequences touch the same STATE_FILE without any locking mechanism.
  Why it fails at runtime: Concurrent poll cycles can race, causing duplicate alerts, lost clock resets, or stale state.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line: _summarize_final_merge_blockers when API fails (lines ~560-590)
  Problem: The function silently returns empty string on API/json errors, so the alert body becomes incomplete.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators receive vague alerts during rate limiting or malformed responses.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line: _pr_required_check_names_for_base (line ~434) and mark_validation_complete call site
  Problem: On a branch-protected ref whose required_status_checks.contexts array is empty, the branch-protection path returns an empty string that is treated as the allow-all sentinel in _pr_checks_completed.
  Why it fails at runtime: A deliberately empty server-side required list is ignored and the code falls back to env var/default behavior.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line: _pr_checks_completed signature (line ~260)
  Problem: The function signature changed from `_pr_checks_completed <PR_NUMBER> [<HEAD_SHA>]` to `_pr_checks_completed <PR_NUMBER> [<HEAD_SHA>] [<BASE_REF>]`, affecting all callers, not just the final merge gate.
  Why it fails at runtime: Wave PR merges now use required-check filtering instead of legacy “all check-runs must pass” behavior, which is a behavioral change.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: agents.md
  Line: line 200
  Problem: New stable log prefix `FINAL_MERGE_INELIGIBILITY_ALERT_SENT` was added without a legacy alias or migration note.
  Why it fails at runtime: Downstream log analysis may miss this new line until updated.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

  Expected change site: tests/test_orchestrate_final_merge_required_checks_gate.py
  Evidence of absence: The test file’s Layer-2 sections use a `long_ago = 0` shortcut and the coverage claim is overstated.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

  Expected change site: Inline comments in _check_final_merge_ineligibility_alert or _clear_final_merge_ineligibility_state
  Evidence of absence: `|| true` is used, but no comment explains the fail-open contract.
